technical_and_design_decisions: Adopt existing Spring Framework patterns: dependency injection, auto-configuration, and the binder abstraction already used in Spring Cloud Stream.
Implement U1 (Azure Event Hubs) as a new Spring Cloud Stream binder on top of the official Azure SDK for Java (com.microsoft.azure:azure-eventhubs), reusing the Kafka binder structure as a template.
Implement U2 (IPython Notebook) via the Jupyter kernel gateway protocol over WebSockets, exposing Spring XD shell commands as a kernel so notebooks can drive the same DSL.
Implement U4 (direct binding) as an in-JVM binder profile that wires producer/consumer modules directly via functional beans, without an external broker.
Implement U5 (REST APIs for xd-admin) using Spring MVC on top of the existing xd-admin server, exposing CRUD endpoints backed by the ModuleRegistry (U6).
Implement U6 (ModuleRegistry stubs) as an in-memory, interface-driven mock that conforms to the existing ModuleRegistry contract, enabling isolated testing of REST endpoints.

Implement U7 (repository migration) as a Git history-preserving move of the spring-cloud-stream-modules project into the spring-cloud-dataflow organization, updating parent POMs, CI configs, and issue links.

Implement U8 (in-memory stream definition repository) as a ConcurrentHashMap-backed implementation of the StreamDefinitionRepository interface, selected via a deployment property to avoid persisting state.

Implement U3 (upgrade preservation) as a migration step in the admin server bootstrap that copies legacy servers.yml and module directories into a versioned backup location before applying the new layout.
assumptions: A single experienced Java/Spring developer will implement all activities (no team parallelism).
The Spring XD and Spring Cloud DataFlow codebases are already available locally and the build infrastructure (Maven/Gradle, CI) is already configured.
Azure Event Hubs credentials and a test namespace are available for development and integration testing.
IPython/Jupyter integration is limited to read/write of the existing Spring XD shell commands; a full notebook UI is out of scope.
The REST API surface for U5 follows the endpoints already informally documented in Spring XD (streams, jobs, modules) and does not introduce a new API contract.
Module migration in U7 keeps Git history using git filter-branch or a similar tool and does not require new module functionality beyond relocation.
One workday equals 8 productive hours; no calendar time, meetings, or onboarding overhead is included.
No major refactor of existing Spring XD core is required; changes are additive or interface-based.

activities.activity_description: Review the eight user stories, identify cross-cutting concerns (U6 feeding U5, U1 binder contract, U4 bypass architecture), produce a short design note covering module/package layout, interface changes, and sequencing of the remaining activities.

activities.activity_name: U1 - Azure Event Hubs binder implementation
activities.activity_description: Create a new spring-cloud-stream-binder-azure-eventhubs module: EventHubsBinderConfiguration, EventHubsMessageChannelBinder, EventHubsProducer, and EventHubsConsumer using the Azure Event Hubs Java SDK, including partition handling, checkpointing, and connection settings.
Add an IPython/Jupyter kernel implementation for the Spring XD shell, expose it through an embedded kernel gateway endpoint, and provide a sample notebook that exercises the XD DSL commands.

activities.activity_name: U3 - Upgrade mechanism preserving legacy configuration
activities.activity_description: Implement an admin-server bootstrap step that detects an existing installation, copies the legacy servers.yml and module directories into a timestamped backup folder, and then applies the new layout so users can manually migrate configuration.

activities.activity_name: U4 - Direct module binding (no messaging middleware)
activities.activity_description: Introduce a 'direct' binder mode that wires producer and consumer modules in the same JVM using a direct in-memory channel, avoiding any external broker; include configuration property, factory bean, and lifecycle handling.

activities.activity_name: U5 - REST APIs for xd-admin CRUD on pipelines
activities.activity_description: Add Spring MVC controllers and DTOs for create/read/update/delete of streams, jobs, and modules, delegating persistence and module resolution to the ModuleRegistry interface (U6) and stream definition repository (U8).

Create an in-memory ModuleRegistry implementation behind the existing ModuleRegistry interface, supporting register, lookup, and unregister of modules so REST endpoints (U5) and tests can be exercised without a real registry.

activities.activity_name: U7 - Move spring-cloud-stream-modules to s-c-d repo
activities.activity_description: Migrate the spring-cloud-stream-modules project into the spring-cloud-dataflow organization: relocate sources while preserving history, update parent POMs, README, CI configuration, and any module coordinate references used by other components.

Implement an InMemoryStreamDefinitionRepository using ConcurrentHashMap that conforms to the StreamDefinitionRepository interface, wire it as an alternative bean activated by a deployment property, and add unit tests.

Run cross-activity integration tests: REST CRUD against the in-memory registry and repository, direct binder round-trip, Azure Event Hubs send/receive against a test namespace (if reachable), and legacy upgrade simulation. Fix any defects uncovered.
Update reference docs (binder configuration for Azure, direct mode, REST endpoints, in-memory repository, upgrade procedure) and address code review comments, finalize Javadoc and changelog entries.
